doneWithoutDeploying.what: All four W10-1 artifacts lower cleanly through the ES executor.
doneWithoutDeploying.whatTheDepCountsSay: The dialog binds a title and reports ZERO state dependencies; the settings screen binds a title AND a scroll offset and reports ONE. Both are the bind-text defect recorded earlier today - KEY_PHASES has no textKey, so a bound title reaches the document and not the manifest. Four real artifacts, and the only bindings that survive lowering are the non-text ones.

notDone.placement: The four files are not in Manta, TSU or SAS. There is no established home for a workbench-generated layout in the consumers, and CLAUDE.md warns against touching TSU's layouts/*.json from a generator - so where they land is a decision, not a mechanical copy.
notDone.buildDeployActualTest: W10-2 wants both jars built and deployed to PrismLauncher 1.21.1(1), plus a dedicated-server run, resource reload, GUI scale, locale, shader-mod and disconnect/reopen. Deploying overwrites jars under a client that may be running and restarting VM-A kicks whoever is on it, so it was left for the user to authorise. Asked, not answered.
notDone.runtimeHashComparison: The browser side of 'browser export hash == loaded runtime program hash' exists for all four - each file's SHA-256 equals the revision hash the page printed. The runtime side needs the jars deployed.

progress2026_08_10_deploy.clientWasNotRunning: Checked as a standalone command before anything else, per the deploy procedure: zero javaw processes. The four java processes were all gradle - two daemons, a worker, and one carrying -Dmanta.consumerCorpus=absent. So there was no client to stop.
progress2026_08_10_deploy.mantaBuilt: gradlew obfuscate produced build/libs/manta-1.1.70-obfuscated.jar. TSU and SAS both pin manta_version 1.1.70, so the artifact matches what they embed.

BLOCKER_FOUND.what: THE PLACEMENT AND THE RUNTIME COMPARISON ARE IN TENSION, and the placement decision settles it against the comparison. /manta6 lab compile takes a RESOURCE ID - Manta6Lab.java line 119, a greedy string argument resolved as a resource - and the four artifacts live in notes/manta6/w10/, which is not on any resource path. Nothing in the runtime can be pointed at them.
BLOCKER_FOUND.soWhatIsAndIsNotVerifiable: The browser half of W10-2's hash comparison is done for all four: each file's SHA-256 equals the revision hash the page printed. The runtime half cannot run at all while the files sit in notes/ - not because a build is missing, but because the loader has no path to them.
BLOCKER_FOUND.andTheJarsWouldNotChange: Worth stating plainly: today's Manta changes are all in browser-workbench/ and notes/, neither of which is packaged, and the consumer changes are notes-only. A rebuilt TSU or SAS jar would carry the same shipped bytes as the deployed one. Deploying would prove nothing about these four artifacts.
BLOCKER_FOUND.whatWouldMakeItVerifiable: Either add the four documents as resources in the consumers - the option that was weighed and not chosen, because it also needs Screen registration and an opening trigger in consumer Java - or give the lab a compile-from-file path so a document outside the resource tree can be lowered and its program hash printed. The second is smaller and is a Manta-side change, which is where W10's subject lives.
